name: @gjsify/webserial
description: Web Serial API for GJS. The Linux backend opens a classic Bluetooth serial port (RFCOMM, SPP) through BlueZ, with no rfcomm binary and no /dev/rfcomm*

scripts.clear: gjsify clear lib tsconfig.tsbuildinfo tsconfig.types.tsbuildinfo test.gjs.mjs
scripts.build: gjsify run build:gjsify && gjsify run build:types
scripts.test: gjsify run build:gjsify && gjsify run build:test && gjsify run test:gjs

osNotes.darwin: The only backend, `BluezRfcommSource`, talks to BlueZ over the system D-Bus, and BlueZ exists on Linux only. On macOS the same `PortSource` seam would be filled by an IOBluetooth driver, which does not exist yet. Until then `navigator.serial` reports no ports there; the package is not usable, so it claims `none` rather than `partial`.
osNotes.win32: The only backend, `BluezRfcommSource`, talks to BlueZ over the system D-Bus, and BlueZ exists on Linux only. There is also no GJS host on Windows at all (ADR 0024 § 4), so the route would be Node with a Windows Bluetooth driver behind the `PortSource` seam, which does not exist yet. The package is not usable on win32 and claims `none`.
